game_fit_scores.rationale: This block-fill satisfaction hook is a casual puzzle/ASMR archetype that has almost zero overlap with Archery Clash's PvP archery dueling loop — there is no aiming, shooting, or character moment to anchor the hook, so users clicking through would face a hard expectation mismatch and likely tank D1 retention. The green/yellow/blue palette is coincidentally adjacent to the game's brand colors, but the flat grid aesthetic clashes with the 3D stylized characters and competitive UI mood. Skip unless the team wants to test a hybrid "fill the bar / power up the shot" reskin that grafts the satisfaction beat onto an actual archery payoff in seconds 3-6.

Hard pass for Archery Clash. The dark noir crime-scene palette (#1a1a2e/brown) and investigative mystery framing clash directly with the game's bright blue/gold competitive PvP energy and stylized female-archer fantasy — there's no narrative bridge to aiming, dueling, or gear collection. Audience overlap is also weak: curiosity/whodunit viewers skew toward narrative puzzle and sim players, not the young-male PvP shooter crowd. Only worth testing if the team can radically reskin the hook (e.g., archer investigating the scene, then drawing a bow), otherwise skip.

The bright blue/high-energy palette and young-male anime audience have some surface overlap with Archery Clash!'s competitive PvP demo, but a Goku Ultra Instinct charge-up has zero connection to aiming/shooting/dueling mechanics and would mislead installs into a bait-and-switch experience. Major frictions: IP/legal risk using Goku likeness, no archery or trajectory hook, and the install intent skews toward anime ARPG fans rather than skill-shot duelers. Skip unless reworked into an original anime-styled archer character showcase that retains the rainbow VFX energy but swaps the charge-sphere for a bow-draw payoff.

brief.title: Ultra Instinct Archer — Rainbow Charge Shot Showcase
brief.hook_3s: Anime-style archer pulls back the bowstring as a crackling blue energy arrow ignites against a pulsing rainbow sky.
scene_flow: 0-3s: Tight close-up on the female archer's eyes glowing electric blue, bowstring drawing back as cyan energy crackles around the arrowhead — rainbow light pulses behind her.
3-7s: Camera whips to over-the-shoulder aiming view; the signature Archery Clash! trajectory arc materializes in gold across a vibrant arena, locking onto a rival duelist's health bar.
7-11s: Release — arrow rips through frame in a streak of blue/yellow/green VFX, slow-mo impact shatters opponent shield, KO banner explodes on screen.
11-14s: Quick montage: rarity-coloured gear cards rain down, bow upgrade tier-up flash (+ATK), level progression bar fills.
14-15s: Hero archer strikes a victory pose against rainbow backdrop, CTA stamp lands.
brief.visual_direction: Lean into Archery Clash!'s 3D stylized cartoonish-but-realistically-lit look, then crank the saturation: bright #2A9DF4 energy auras around the bow, #FFD700 trajectory arc and damage numbers, #32CD32 rarity glows on dropped gear. Rainbow gradient skybox borrowed from the anime archetype but grounded in the game's existing arena geometry, banners, and HUD chrome. Energetic/competitive pacing — fast cuts, screen-shake on release, anime-style speed lines on the arrow streak. Female protagonist stays on-model with current in-game character, no Goku likeness.
brief.rationale: Voodoo's current Archery Clash! rotation is dominated by silent playables and a self-aware "I paid for this ad" video — there is zero high-energy anime/VFX character-showcase angle in their mix, despite the audience skewing young male anime-adjacent. This brief imports the trending rainbow charge-up hook from the market scan but legally reskins it onto the game's own female archer with a bow-draw payoff, solving the IP risk while filling the showcase gap. UA should A/B this against the existing playable-heavy lineup on Applovin/Admob to capture anime-leaning installs the current creatives miss.
